newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - GAN shares soar on rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - GAN shares soar on rescue plan.

text.p: Shares in Groupe des Assurances Nationales rocketed on Friday as investors bet the government's 20 billion franc ($3.5 billion) rescue of the state-controlled insurer would return it to profit and make it a bid target.

The share soared 21.22 percent to 150 francs before being suspended in early afternoon. Several attempts to requote were abandoned after the share repeatedly surged through price barriers, triggering the halt in trading.
The shares would requote on Friday only if they stayed under a ceiling of 149.10 francs, the SBF stock markets association said.
"The market is betting that cleaned up of its property problems and (property) losses, GAN will be profitable again," said a Paris analyst.
Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) ran up massive losses in recent years on property loans and insurance underwriting.
The bailout is the latest in a string of hugely expensive state mop-up operations in France's financial sector.
Trading in the shares was suspended at 123 francs on Thursday ahead of the announcement of the rescue package.

"Obviously the market's assumption is that the government is pretty much writing out a blank cheque," one insurance analyst said. "It's philanthropy on the part of the government which given the extent of the bailout seems to surprising."

But while expensive, GAN's rescue was not expected, to prove as costly as the salvage of state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais, whose lending romp in the 1980s could land taxpayers with a bill of more 100 billion francs.
Underpinning the GAN share price rise, an analyst said, was the assumption that a clean GAN, shorn of its property troubles, would be a much more palatable bid target.
The government said it planned to privatise GAN and CIC, the regional banking group it controls, this year if possible.
Such a move is seen as a pre-condition of approval by the European Commission for the aid. The Commission announced on Friday it would investigate the new rescue plan.

Speculation has resurfaced in the stock market recently that consolidation in the sector could mean more mergers, with some traders suggesting the possibility of a bid for GAN by rival private French insurer AGF.

Some analysts boosted their recommendations to "buy" from "sell" on the strength of the rescue plan under which the state will inject 11 billion francs in capital in 1997 and give guarantees against future losses in GAN's property portfolio estimated at nine billion francs.
The new money comes on top of 2.9 billon francs in state aid already supplied to GAN in 1995.

Dealers said one Paris brokerage had boosted its 1997 profit forecast from a loss of 3.3 francs per share to a profit of 15 francs per share and for 1998, was looking for a profit of 17 francs compared with an earlier estimate of 7.3 francs.
The group said on Thursday it expected to announce a five billion franc loss for 1996 after a 1.78 billion loss in 1995.

The rescue includes plans to provide seven billion francs to cover losses at GAN's UIC property unit which has run up losses of 30 billion francs in three years and 3.9 billion francs for GAN Assurances which had been hit by poor underwriting results. ($ = 5.708 French Francs)
